WHAT YOU ANSWER

21 everyday statements.
Three for each tendency.

Our original questions describe situations such as receiving feedback, comparing a milestone, replying to a rude message, or beginning an awkward task. Each is assigned to one of the seven tendencies. All three questions within a tendency carry equal weight.

Choose how much the statement sounds like your usual self. Use the same interpretation of “usual” throughout rather than trying to produce a particular character.

The five answer choices
AnswerSelected value
Not like me0
A little like me1
Somewhat like me2
Mostly like me3
Very like me4

FROM ANSWERS TO NUMBERS

One formula,
used seven times.

Two questions per tendency describe the tendency directly. Their selected values count as points. One question describes a balancing response. For that reverse-scored question, points equal 4 minus the selected value.

Direct question: points = selected valueBalancing question: points = 4 − selected valueDisplayed score: round(total ÷ 12 × 100)

Add the three question scores to get a raw total from 0 to 12. Divide by 12, multiply by 100, and round to the nearest whole number. Repeat separately for all seven tendencies. No other tendency’s score changes that denominator.

The reverse-scored item is not a lie detector and carries no extra weight. It allows a balancing statement to contribute in the opposite direction on the same scale.

FOLLOW ONE SCORE

A worked pride example.

Suppose these are the selected values for the three pride questions. The middle question describes accepting a better approach, so its selected value is reversed before adding.

Illustrative answers, not your result
SituationSelected valuePoints counted
The team gets a compliment.Direct statement33
Someone suggests a better way.Balancing statement14 − 1 = 3
You realize you got a detail wrong.Direct statement22
Raw total8 / 12

8 ÷ 12 × 100 = 66.67…Rounded pride score: 67 / 100

The other six tendencies are calculated from their own answers in exactly the same way. This example does not set a threshold for a “prideful person.”

HOW WE CHOOSE THE HEADLINE

The highest score leads.
Equal highest scores share it.

A single highest score gets one leading character. If two or more tie for highest, the result shows every tied leader. If all seven match, the headline is Even Ensemble. Nothing breaks a genuine tie.

The next lower score may appear as a close contender. It is context for your profile, not a validated second personality type. See the three example results to compare these displays.

You must answer all 21 statements before the quiz generates a result. Incomplete answers are not filled in or guessed.

How does this compare with the IDRlabs 7 deadly sins test?

If you have taken other versions, the most obvious difference is the scoring. Many quizzes return one label; this one scores all seven tendencies separately and shows the close contenders. The 21 statements here were written for this project, every question uses the same answer scale, and the full calculation is published above. Seven Little Sins is not affiliated with IDRlabs and does not use their questions, so scores from the two tests are not directly comparable.

WHAT THE QUIZ CAN AND CANNOT DO

A reflection tool.
With clear limits.

Seven Little Sins is an original entertainment quiz. We have not established scientific validity, representative norms, diagnostic thresholds, or test–retest reliability for these questions. The scores are neither population percentiles nor measures of moral worth.

Three questions cannot capture all the reasons behind a behavior. Rest, attraction, ambition, anger, and enjoying things are ordinary experiences. The quiz cannot assess mental health, sexuality, eating behavior, or the circumstances affecting your energy and choices.

The names draw on a traditional set of vices, but the characters, everyday framing, and questions belong to this site. This is not the IDRlabs test and is not an anime character matcher. Read the overview of the seven names for that distinction.

WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR ANSWERS

Scored on your device.

The quiz calculates results in your browser. Your attempt and latest result are saved in this tab’s session storage so that refreshing can preserve progress. Start over clears the attempt. If storage is unavailable, the quiz can still run, but a refresh may lose progress.

Answers and scores are not sent to a quiz server. When enabled, GA4 measures page visits and engagement; our analytics code excludes quiz answers, scores, result fragments, and arbitrary query values. The privacy notice explains storage and analytics.

A shared result link includes seven scores after #. Anyone who receives the link can view them. The downloadable character PNG omits the score chart. Read what each sharing option contains before choosing one.

Can I compare my result with the IDRlabs test?

You can take both, but the scores are not on the same scale — a 70 here does not mean a 70 there. This page explains exactly how the numbers here are produced.
